articles.title: I’m 50 years old. Why do I still struggle with the need to be liked?
articles.summary: An over-investment in people-pleasing can be emotionally costly. Here’s how I’m training myself to be OK with letting people down. A few months ago, my 10-year-old daughter and I went to our neighborhood cafe. At the counter, the owner greeted us with her typical effusion of warmth and welcome.
body: My face flushed. I was embarrassed and incensed by what I perceived as blatant rudeness. You could at least smile, I thought.

When we left, I pulled my daughter aside and gave her a firm talk about respect and manners, but her face dropped and she looked like she might cry. I quickly realized that she was in a bad mood, and totally unaware of her external affect. I felt bad for not approaching the conversation differently – I had assumed she recognized her impoliteness, that she was taking a stab at playing “sulky irreverent teen”.

That’s when it hit me: by dictating that she should comport herself contrary to how she was actually feeling, I was reinforcing society’s attempts to mold girls and women into automatons who reflexively try to please everyone but themselves. It’s ironic, because I had written an entire book to warn her about doing just that: Ugly: A Letter to My Daughter. I knew these types of messages often lead to what psychologist Mary Pipher writes about in Reviving Ophelia: a “split self” that often results in the creation of a “false self” in line with gendered expectations.
points: An over-investment in people-pleasing can be emotionally costly.
Here’s how I’m training myself to be OK with letting people down.

articles.title: ‘A feudal relationship’: Stonegate Pub Partners under scrutiny after complaints of tenant mistreatment
articles.summary: UK’s largest pub company with the lowest satisfaction rating accused of entrapping landlords into financial loss situations. “We’re pleased to welcome Stonegate Pub Partners as a sponsor for the Great British Pub Awards 2026” read a post on the event’s Facebook page.
body: “Must be 1st April again,” said one commenter. “This is like Pontius Pilate being appointed child welfare ambassador,” said another. Other comments about the UK’s largest pub company were significantly less polite.

Days earlier, Stonegate had been named as the subject of an investigation by the industry regulator, the Pubs Code Adjudicator (PCA) over alleged mistreatment of the tenants who run more than 3,000 of its venues.

Melissa Phillips’s father, known locally as “Phil”, was one of them. After taking over a more or less derelict venue in Basingstoke, Hampshire, he renamed it Laarsen’s, an anagram of his beloved Arsenal FC, and turned it into a highly successful football pub that the company cited to trainee publicans as a success story.

But after he began suffering from the effects of Alzheimer’s, he lost his ability to keep on top of the business. “He would pay bills twice or not at all and would sometimes fall asleep during meetings with the area sales manager,” said Melissa.
points: UK’s largest pub company with the lowest satisfaction rating accused of entrapping landlords into financial loss situations.

articles.title: I'm prone to spills. The Owala SmoothSip Slider is the only travel coffee mug I trust
articles.summary: Owala’s SmoothSip coffee mug keeps drinks as hot (or as cold) as I like, without making a mess. Yeti Rambler v Owala FreeSip: which trendy water bottle actually deserves the hype? Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I refuse to drink mediocre coffee. After about two months at my internship office, drinking the cheap, bitter, and acidic blends that were available to me, I now prefer the soy latte I make at home and would like (with my trusty Moka Pot ) to bring it with me wherever I go.

Yet carrying a thermos full of coffee came with a risk: would my MacBook, notebooks and lunch emerge dripping with coffee, forcing me to fork over $1,000 and spend $20 on an overpriced salad? Or, would my belongings emerge miraculously unscathed and dry?

I had been burned in the past, putting a thermos full of coffee into my backpack’s drink holder, only to discover that half of its contents spilled while running to catch the bus or rushing to work. This was not a sustainable situation, so a few years ago, I replaced my old hand-me-down Contigo thermos with the SmoothSip from Owala, a brand we’ve recommended, known for its leakproof, colorful water bottles. The promise was that its SmoothSip coffee tumbler was leakproof – and what a relief to learn that their claim turned out to be true.
points: Owala’s SmoothSip coffee mug keeps drinks as hot (or as cold) as I like, without making a mess.

articles.title: Inside Jordyn Woods and Karl-Anthony Towns’s Classic Wedding Weekend in Malibu
articles.summary: After six years together, the model-entrepreneur and New York Knicks star exchanged vows at a private estate overlooking the Pacific, with custom Danielle Frankel for the bride and Ralph Lauren for the groom.
body: On Saturday, August 15, model and entrepreneur Jordyn Woods and New York Knicks center and NBA champion Karl-Anthony Towns married surrounded by family and friends at a private home overlooking the ocean in Malibu.

The couple first met nine years ago in Los Angeles, in 2017, where Karl was spending his off-season and where Jordyn grew up. “We connected over a game of Uno, and he thinks that he won,” Jordyn remembers. “We both have a very competitive nature. When we play games, we are not on the same team—we are in it to win.”

The two became close and were good friends for two years before they eventually started dating in 2020. “I lost my dad at 19,” Jordyn says. “And during COVID, his mom got sick and passed, and I was able to be there for him in a different way.”

articles.title: How to Style Wide-Leg Jeans, According to the Street-Style Set
articles.summary: Wide-leg jeans are one of the most popular denim trends, and this is how to style yours, with inspiration straight from the street style set.
body: Over the past few years, denim trends have been a particularly hot topic here at Vogue HQ. From the divisive barrel leg and ultra-low-rise styles, to the return of skinny jeans, there has been no shortage of denim shapes to debate—and, in many cases, internet discourses to fuel. For 2026, however, the denim styles leading the conversation feel, by comparison, reassuringly familiar.

“Straight-leg and high-waisted cuts from the spring/summer 2026 collections didn’t stray far from classic shapes, with enduring qualities that exist beyond the seasonal trend cycle,” Vogue ’s Alice Cary noted in her guide to this year’s denim styles, spotlighting failsafe fits like the classic straight-leg, cropped and slightly wide-leg as standouts for 2026.
points: Wide-leg jeans are one of the most popular denim trends, and this is how to style yours, with inspiration straight from the street style set.

articles.title: You Can Now Use Whoop's Blood Tests Without a Membership
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Whoop, the company best known for its screen-free fitness band, continues to expand its domain in the broader healthcare space.
body: Since Whoop launched Advanced Labs last fall, you needed a Whoop membership in order to connect your blood test results with the company's continuous health monitoring in the Whoop app. Now the lab testing stands on its own as a direct-to-consumer product—continuing the trend of companies like Whoop wanting to grow beyond "wearables" into comprehensive, one-stop-shop health platforms.

The newly added Galleri test works a bit differently. It's a single blood draw that screens for a signal shared across more than 50 cancer types, many of which have no standard screening protocol today. To be clear, it detects a signal suggesting cancer may be present, not a diagnosis, and it's meant to supplement the screenings your doctor already recommends, not replace them. Advanced Labs isn't currently covered by insurance, though purchases may qualify for HSA or FSA reimbursement, which you should confirm with your plan administrator before you buy.

articles.title: Steak au Poivre (Strip Steak With Creamy Peppercon Sauce)
articles.summary: Fulfill your 10 p.m. Parisian dinner dreams with a deeply seared steak drenched in creamy cognac-peppercorn sauce.
body: A great steak au poivre is all about contrast: deeply browned steak, a silky cream sauce, and enough cracked black pepper to cut through all that richness. This version, adapted from Molly Baz’s Cook This Book, pairs thick-cut New York strip steaks with a quick pan sauce of cognac, heavy cream, shallot, garlic, and plenty of coarsely crushed peppercorns.

For the best crust, pat the steaks dry and leave them undisturbed when they first hit the hot skillet ( Watch video: How to Sear Steak the Right Way ). Fresh peppercorns matter too: Crushing them coarsely rather than grinding them finely gives the sauce its signature peppery bite and crunch. Once the steaks are resting, use the same skillet—and all those flavorful browned bits—to build the sauce.

Keep an eye on the cream once it goes in. It only needs to simmer briefly, until the sauce is glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon. Then slice the steak against the grain, return any juices from the cutting board to the pan, and spoon that peppery sauce generously over top.
Try this recipe with this expert pick from the Bon Appétit Wine Shop.
points: Parisian dinner dreams with a deeply seared steak drenched in creamy cognac-peppercorn sauce.
